Uniform Title: Unmattabhairava Manuscript: IFP/EFEO Transcript T1020 Description: Rites and Mantras Relating to Unmatta Bhairava
The Ecstatic Bhairava (Udbhaṭabhairava). He is one of a group of eight Bhairavas, of which Svacchandabhairava is the most well known. Manuals for the other Bhairavas have not yet been traced.
Notes: Data entered by the staff of Muktabodha under the supervision of Mark S.G. Dyczkowski. Revision 0: April 8, 2012.
Country of publication: India.
The Heart of Unmattabhairava.
Homage to Śrī Gaṇeśa.
Oṃ, homage to Śiva.
Oṃ, homage to Unmattabhairava!
The venerable Dakṣiṇāmūrti said:
Listen, O fortunate Rudra, compassionate one, supreme among men; listen with an attentive mind to Unmattabhairava, the bearer of the Yantra. 1.
The seed-syllable of Lakṣmī in the form of a liṅga, the fragments, the breaks, the three pairs, the banner,
the foot-mark, and Māyā, which is revealed through the four paths.
It is measured by moats, provided with a central square marked by a dot,
and in its center, it is adorned with a row of *muṇḍa* figures representing the form of Śeṣa.
She is encircled by the great nāga Vāsuki, bears the mark of a thunderbolt,
is surrounded by weapons, stones, and missiles, and is endowed with chowries.
[He saw] Lakṣmī, adorned with various weapons and a bell, endowed with circular gates,
accompanied by Bhairava and other yantras, and a woman radiant with desire.
O Śaṅkara, listen to these well-known yantras of Bhairavī, which are always joined with the seed-syllable *varavarṇā* and the letter *ra*, and which are complete and great. 6.
The best of practitioners should wear that which is written with red sandalwood for the purpose of killing and destroying enemies; one should write it with the blood of cats.
In rites of subjugation, one should write with the flow of a woman's menstrual blood;
likewise in rites of expulsion, insanity, delusion, and when afflicted by enemies. (8)
The practitioner, having purified himself, should write that [mantra] upon a birch-bark leaf with lotus-ink;
it is the sole rule for those who offer separate *bali* offerings.
For the purpose of killing, one should have a fish sacrificed in a cremation ground at the onset of night;
however, at the time of destroying an enemy, one should offer a black sheep.
In rites for subjugation and delusion, I shall kill a cat for you;
in rites for expulsion and madness, I shall kill a pig for you.

At night, the great lord Yantrarāja performs the worship of Bhairava with various kinds of meat, including the three sections [of the sacrificial victim] combined with fish, meat, and other offerings.
Whether it be through worship, devotion, or desire for a specific fruit, one should wear that wheel which grants success; she is the beautiful Maramānanda.
For the easy understanding of the ignorant, [this work describes] where the Great-Souled King of Yoga is afflicted by his own wheels or by the wheels of others, or by Ḍaṅkinī and the rest.
For the purpose of destroying madness and misfortune, one should worship Bhairava,
offering a goat as a sacrificial oblation (bali) and partaking of the Vāruṇī liquor.
O Śiva, if the King of Machines (yantrarāja) should become obstructed in its many functions,
one should perform worship according to the rules and offer the causal oblation (balim).
Thus concludes the extraction of the Unmattabhairava Yantra; may it be auspicious. Om. Salutations to Śrī Gaṇeśa.
Oṃ, homage to Unmattabhairava.
Śrī Dakṣiṇāmūrti said: The Kīlaka of the Lord of Lords consists of three Vedas together with the Yati; Maheśvara is the king of mantras of the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma Vedas. (1)
Through the mantras of the *paryeṣaṇās*, humans shall possess the divine eye;
through the mantras possessing the power of lightning, there is the *kīlaka* among various mantras.
Bhairava [is that] which, having torn asunder the sin of Bhairava and the sin of sin,
exists for the sake of various liberations and for the sake of diverse purposes within the states of existence and non-existence.
On the new moon day, the fourteenth, the tenth, and likewise the twelfth,
the best of worshippers should contemplate the hostility of Anurādhā.
Month after month, fortnight after fortnight, with the most excellent auspicious rites,
during the months of Vaiśākha, Phālguna, Māgha, Kārttika, and Mārgaśīrṣa.
The two dark fortnights are divided by other months;
through the streams [of breath] in the midst of the seven, they are distinguished by the Sun and the Moon.
Whether it be killing, deluding, subjugation, striking, or combined with expulsion—if the Guru should worship [the deity] separately for these purposes, [he incurs fault]. || 7 ||

In the state of meditative concentration, Viśvāmitra and the two Bhāradvājas entered the sacrificial post that had been established by the sage Vasiṣṭha, who was possessed of mastery and accessible through meditation.
(4) You alone are the established *kīlaka*; you are the *kīlaka* of the mindless ones. Having made yourself the *kīlaka* of all, [you are] the *kīlaka* by means of Bhānucandra. 9.
Therefore, O compassionate Rudra, one should always recite or wear this *dhāraṇakīlaka* according to the prescribed rules, along with the most excellent hymns to the *yantra*.
This is the doctrine of the great-souled Bhairava Kīlaka;
O Śaṅkara, listen again to the majesty of the armor (kavaca) in detail. || 11 ||
Thus ends the *Śrī-Unmattabhairavakīlaka*. May there be auspiciousness! Now, the mudrās:
the *sumukha*, the *saṃpuṭa*, the *vitata*, and likewise the *vistara*.
She holds the great goad and the great meat, and is endowed with the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness. || 1 ||
One should display the fish, tortoise, boar, and cow mudrās;
these are the twelve mudrās by which the ritual action is performed as a morsel [of offering]. (2) May it be auspicious.
Homage to Śrī Gaṇeśa.
Oṃ, homage to Unmattabhairava!
Śrī Mahādeva said:
O Guru, Lord of the worlds, Kavi, the Bhārgava of the three realms, tiger among Brahmanical sages and munis, king of that place, and lord of the ṛṣis! || 1 ||
The wise Unmattabhairava is of a wondrous form among names;
he is shameless, supreme bliss, of terrible aspect, and fearsome. || 2 ||
Then, its arising occurs; what is it that illuminates the effect within the cause?
O Lord, I wish to hear about that, along with its five limbs and its fruits. (3)
I speak because I am pleased; how could I be mad? O Bhairavas, what [portion] of the mantras and tantras should be introduced at what time? (4)
"O Lord of speakers, having seen your disciple, you are filled with grace; you are entirely without remainder [in your compassion].
Having spoken thus, Lokeśa stood before the Guru.
He joined his palms in reverence and bowed down again and again;
for by the Teacher of the three worlds, the entire universe becomes blessed in an instant.
The venerable Dakṣiṇāmūrti said:
Listen, O disciple of great intelligence, to these words of one who is gratified by devotion—the words of her who is worshipped by the gods of gods. "O servant of Bhava, you are blessed. (7)
O Maheśvara, through the elevation of supreme bliss, the wise one has brought about the mind; first, hear the twelve names.

Om. For this *mūlamantra* consisting of the twelve names of the venerable Unmattabhairava, whose form is supreme bliss (*paramānandamūrti*), the seer (*ṛṣi*) is Nemunya and others; the meters (*chandas*) are the *Ṛg*, *Yajur*, *Sāma*, and *Atharva*; and the deity (*devatā*) is the venerable Unmattabhairava.
Oṃ! The seed-syllable is supreme bliss; the Unmattas are the power (śakti); Bhīmā, Ḍākinī, and the others are the kīlaka for destruction.
This is the application (viniyoga) for recitation for the sake of attaining the fourfold aims of human life, excluding [the pursuit of] honey, meat, and so forth.
Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to the two thumbs; Oṃ paramānanda hrīṃ, svāhā to the two index fingers.
Oṃ, to the deity Unmattabhairava, vaṣaṭ with the two middle fingers.
Oṃ, for the warding off of defects such as those caused by ḍākinīs and others, hūṃ with the two ring fingers, hūṃ.
Oṃ, to the shameless one of terrifying form, vauṣaṭ to the two little fingers.
Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ, to the one whose form is supreme bliss, praṃ praṃ praṃ; [grant] my *lavarayīṃ*, hrīṃ;
to Unmattabhairava, hūṃ; with the palms and backs of the hands, phaṭ. Having thus performed the ritual placements (*nyāsa*) on the heart and other parts, one should prostrate like a staff.
Om, the first is named Unmatta, and the second is likewise Bhairava.
The third is Bhīmarūpā, and the fourth is Yoginīpati.
The fifth is Mātṛkānātha, and the sixth is Nirlajja;
the seventh is Paramānanda, and the eighth is Aṣṭabhairava. 10.
The ninth is Gaṇanātha, and the tenth is Ḍākinīhata;
the eleventh is named Ghora, and the twelfth is Sātvikī. (11)
These are the twelve names [of] Unmattabhairava Hara;
O disciple, listen as I shall proclaim that heart-mantra, O Maheśvara. (12)

Hari Oṃ Tatsat. In the Pārameśvara Tantra, in the Vārāṇasī Paṭala, within the narrative of Śrī Unmattabhairava, in the dialogue between the Guru and Rudra, here ends the auspicious Śrī Unmattabhairava Stotra. || 2972 ||
Om, salutation to Unmattabhairava. The illustrious Dakṣiṇāmūrti said:
The wise Unmattabhairava—listen indeed to his heart-essence.
O Lord of Gods, O Hara, I shall tell you this secret which was spoken by you.
O Rudra, the heart of Bhairava, accompanied by the mantra, shall always grant the fulfillment of one's desires and the origin of Bhairava.
In a former age, when [the conflict] arose, Hari assumed the form of a Buddha; his power, possessing a contrary body, brought about the destruction of the lineage in the world. (3)
O Rudra, the third among them was indeed a son, while his daughter was a woman named Ḍaṅkiṇī; each by their respective names, they were the destroyers of the children of the three worlds.
May Dhūmramātaṅginī, awakened, grant me the protection of a Buddha;
by the name of the eldest son of Ḍaṅkinī, he became Dhūmralocana. || 5 ||
Dhānyamālin is the eldest daughter, Dhūmrabīja is the little finger;
Dhūmrinī is indeed her sister, and Vakabandha is the little toe. (6)
Listen at the end of this narration; hear the six names.
Together with his two mothers, he shall possess a lineage throughout the seven worlds.
O Rudra, you who assume the form of a madman, I am afflicted by [the suffering] of Brāhmaṇas, Kṣatriyas, and Vaiśyas, along with their sons and daughters; therefore, have compassion! 8.
Shameless and devoid of ego, being naturally separated from you,
I do not know by what means I shall hear my own flesh in the city.
The entire world transcends illusion, yet you are born from illusion;
listen, O disciple, for your play is that of the Great-Souled Mattabhairava.

Oṃ. Of this *hṛdaya-mūlamantra* of the illustrious *Unmattabhairava*, the seer (*ṛṣi*) is Vyāghravadana Bhairava, the meter (*chandas*) is the pair of tigers (*śārdūladvandva*), the deity (*devatā*) is the illustrious *Unmattabhairava*, the seed-syllables (*bīja*) are RĀṂ RĀṂ RĀṂ LAṂ VAṂ, the power (*śakti*) is TRĀṂ TRĀṂ TRĀṂ EṂ HUṂ HUṂ HUṂ HĀ HĀ HĀ, and the pin (*kīlaka*) is the human [state] for the destruction of fear and suffering, [granting] the fourfold aims of human life (*caturvidha-puruṣārtha*).
The application [of this mantra] is for the purpose of attaining accomplishment and for the purpose of warding off defects such as those caused by *ḍākinīs* during recitation.
Oṃ Rāṃ Phrūṃ Pamalavarayīṃ, homage to the eastern form! Huṃ!
oṃ tāṃ aiṃ amalavarayīṃ, obeisance to the Āgneya Mūrti. Huṃ.
Oṃ āṃ jaṃ, homage to the embodiment of bliss, the supreme lotus-lady; jrūṃ, homage to the embodiment of Yama. Huṃ!
Oṃ Taḥ Taḥ Taḥ Trīṃ Trīṃ Tamalavarayīṃ Naiḥ; obeisance to the Nairṛta-form! Hūṃ!
oṃ vrāṃ vāhane vrūṃ vamalavarayīṃ, salutation to the form of Varuṇa! huṃ!
oṃ maṃ mārute mrāiṃ mrāiṃ mamalavarayīṃ, obeisance to the one whose form is of great majesty, to the one whose form is the wind.
Huṃ.
oṃ & kraṃ kraṃ kraṃ kā kā kā kāruṇi kuhu kuhu kuhu hrīṃ dhamalavarayīṃ dhaḥ, obeisance to the embodiment of Dhaneśvara.
Huṃ īṃ, phaṭ! To the form of Īśāna, the form of the Mother of Mantras, īṃ bha ma la va ra yīṃ, to Paśupati, hrīṃ īṃ, to the form of Īśāna, obeisance! Huṃ!
Oṃ! Salutations to the Lord of Splendors; salutations. From the ether: Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Akasavarīṃ Āṃ. Salutations to the one whose form is the ether.
Huṃ.
Oṃ adho āntarikṣe kalaśrī antarīkṣam antarīkṣamūrtaye namaḥ | Hūṃ |
Oṃ bhrūṃ adha bhaṃ alavara hūṃ, homage to the lower form (adhamūrti) huṃ!

I perpetually bow to Nārācī, who is surrounded by a host of ḍākinīs that destroy obstacles; she whose form is blissful, whose nature is matted locks, who is the beloved of Sadāśiva in solitude, and who assumes various forms. O Lord of the Gods, I constantly prostrate before her who is adorned with swaying tawny matted locks, who is free from shame, the destroyer of fear, and whose husband is Hara, the Boar-faced one (Vārāha).
Thus is the initial meditation; now follows the sixfold ritual placement (ṣoḍhānyāsa).
Oṃ śīṃ śamalavarayīṃ, svāhā to the head.

Oṃ śrīṃ śrīṃ śrama-lava-rahrīṃ! O you named Śrī-Unmattānandamūrti, mama-lava-rayīṃ! Protect, protect the binding of the directions!

OṂ BHRĀṂ, salutation to Bhairava with the palms and backs of the hands; OṂ ĀNANDAMŪRTAYE SVABHĀVARAHITĀYA, salutation to the embodiment of bliss who is devoid of inherent nature with the two little fingers; OṂ VRĀṂ VĀRĀHIPATAYE VRŪṂ, salutation with the two ring fingers.

oṃ hūṃ, obeisance to the two tarjanī fingers of the Ḍākinī who destroys pride, hūṃ taṃ.
Obeisance to the one whose form is of wondrous appearance, who shatters all fears; to the two thumbs, *namaḥ*.
Oṃ, for the destruction of ghosts, spirits, and demons, for the shattering of fear, to the guardian of the directions: Hrīṃ, the binding of the quarters.
Phaṭ hūṃ! To Bhairavanātha, the weapon-mantra, phaṭ!
Hrīṃ to the twelve-armed one who bears arms, to the crusher of enemies, huṃ to the armor, huṃ!
Mraṃ mrūṃ to the one of manifold forms, svāhā to the head in the long meter!
Thus is the ritual placement (nyāsa).
I bow to the Lord of the Mother, who is accompanied by the Mistress of Flames, the Preceptor of the Gods, who dances, and who has shattered the beloved of Hara along with his bliss and fearlessness.
Six times the pair of *huṃ*s for the beloved.

Having bowed to the Guru Bhairava, who has subdued the boar-faced goddess Vārāhī, who is the Lord of Beasts (Paśupati), who has destroyed the Ḍākinīs, and who removes the fear of the intoxicated, I praise him who utters the sound of the universe.
Thus is the meditation:

Oṃ Śrīṃ, may we know Unmattabhairava; may we meditate upon Him who is devoid of inherent nature; may Bhava Rudra inspire us. Oṃ, may we know Bhīmeśvara; may we meditate upon Lambakara; may Māna Indra inspire us.
Oṃ hrīṃ! We know Ānanda; we meditate upon Ratnamukuṭa; may the one free from shame inspire us. This is the Gāyatrī.
Now, the root mantra: Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ! Unmattabhairava, huṃ phaṭ! Destroy the power of the wicked ḍākinīs; grant me fearlessness.
2 huṃ! Kill, kill the ḍākinī! Svāhā!
Having recited four hundred times the Gāyatrī mantra together with the *Sambhava-mantra*,
one should do so in a forest, a cremation ground, or in the sacred field of Vārāṇasī.
Having recited it eighty lakhs of times, one becomes a wish-fulfilling gem for the mind; likewise, with beads of pearl, coral, rudrākṣa, or excellent crystal [the result is attained]. (2)
The best [initiation] consists of a gold pill, the middling of a silver pill;
listen, the state of being a disciple [is established] by garlands woven from woolen threads. (3)
The cow-faced [vessel] is limited in size and is of the most excellent black color;
listen now to the description of the seat for practitioners, which consists of wool, a purifier, and cloth. (4)
The best [seat] should be made of human skin, with an elephant's footprint in its center;
that of tiger skin is middling, and the lowest is made of deer skin.
O Rudra, O best of men, you should listen in detail to the procedure for the worship of Bhairava, which must be performed by practitioners.
Having brought water from the Gaṅgā according to the ritual procedure and with a firm resolve,
those excellent women performed the worship of Bhīma during the midnight hours.
Alone, accompanied by his disciples, he praised the excellent incense, which was blended with *śrīkhaṇḍa* sandalwood and combined with red sandalwood. (8)
She was endowed with the splendor of vermilion, anointed with various fragrant unguents,
possessed of beautiful eyes, adorned with banners, and arrayed in diverse garments.
With unbroken grains, she should have a dark complexion and be joined with barley and sesame;
her body should be encircled by a black thread consisting of nine strands.
Her limbs were adorned with various wonderful flowers, fragrant and most enchanting,
colored by hibiscus, kaṅkola, mālatī, pārijāta, and other blossoms.
She consists of the essence of nectar, fragrant and full of the essence of ambrosia;
her form is composed of the moon and sun, a captivating embodiment of splendor. (12)
Having performed worship with divine offerings joined with gold and accompanied by incense and lamps, he gave food to Bhairava of terrifying form.
O God, when one offers the food offering (naivedya) even once, consisting of various kinds of cooked foods endowed with various flavors, Hara is truly offered to.
The Lord Sun is pleased by an offering of various fruits, including sugarcane, oranges, plantains, and sweet mangoes.
O God, one should offer the *arghya* with libations that are sweet and intoxicating, with the three kinds of *hrīṃ* seeds,
with camphor, and with the nectar of milk.
One should indeed offer betel nuts, betel leaves, and beautiful items such as catechu wood,
as well as gold, silver, copper, and a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā).
Then he performed the *puṣpāñjali* hymn, offered honey and food,
and conducted the worship according to the rules, while the preceptor was being honored.
Oṃ! Salutations to the god Rudra, the lord of beings;
salutations again and again to Bhava, to Narasiṃha, and to the Madman. || 19 ||
Homage to Bhairava, the Lord of the World, homage to the Master of the worlds! Homage to the Lord of the three worlds, homage to the Master of all beings! || 20 ||

Having recited [the mantra] thus, one should offer parched grain (lājā) for fulfillment and incense consisting of *gulālaka* and *guggulu* for pervasion, while performing the recitation (*japa*) according to the prescribed ritual rules. (21)
The syllable Oṃ is devotion to Śiva, which pervades the three worlds and the universe;
the syllable Aiṃ is Kāmarāja, conjoined with the pursuit of desire.
The seed-syllable conjoined with Bhairavī is Bhairavī; she pervades the universe. Hrīṃ is the Māyā-bīja, the seed of the Mātṛkās, endowed with the abode of the gods. (23)
Through the mantras beginning with the seed-syllable *hrīṃ*, the pervasion of Gaurī and the others throughout the universe is declared;
may the Creator of the Universe, the Lord of the Universe (*Viśveśvara*), be praised. (24)
Having bowed to Mahālakṣmī, who pervades the seed-syllable of Lakṣmī and all else—Mahālakṣmī, the seed of the universe, who pervades the entire world. (25)
The letter *na* and the letter *ma*—Viṣṇu and Indra—shall dwell there in happiness;
thereafter, all [the gods] shall be present through the two Kumāras, the Aśvins, and the physicians of the gods.
The seed-syllable *Bhaṃ* is the remover of fear and is itself Bhairava-Bhānumān; when combined with the syllable *Aiṃ*, it is called *Bhaiṃ*. || 27 ||
The seed-syllable of the Sun-god is the nature of the Sun; likewise, the seed-syllable of Varuṇa is the syllable *va* joined with the syllable *oṃ*; these two constitute a pair of couples.
HŪṂ—by means of the wrathful deities with black bodies, accompanied by the *anusvāra*, the letters *da* and *u* are for the [deities of] attachment; the letter *du* is the Yoginīs themselves. (29)
Having joined the letter *sa* and the letter *ta* of the two pairs of syllables,
and having combined Bhava with Māyā along with the *ta*-letters, one becomes Śiva himself.
The Mātṛkā herself, beginning with the letter *da*, is bound together with the seed-syllables (*bīja*);
likewise, the group beginning with *i*, along with the initial groups of letters, constitutes Sarasvatī.
The consonant groups accompanied by the vowel *ī*, and the letter *na*, are the supreme seed-syllables (*bīja*). The water-seed (*vāribīja*) is the letter *ni* joined with the four oceans.
The seed-syllable of the *tavarga* (the dental class) is associated with the lunar days (tithis) numbered nineteen;
the Moon himself is Brahmā, the Brāhmaṇa, and the best of kings.
The seed-syllable *aiṃ* was joyfully uttered together with the letter *a*;
it was joined with the *ja*-group of consonants, meritorious, and endowed with victory and auspiciousness.
The ninefold group, together with its forms, has Nṛtyadaivatā as its deity;
the goddess is Sakārasundarī, and Yakāra is indeed Pārvatī. (35)
The letter *ma* is Mahālakṣmī, and likewise the letter *mā* is Kālikā;
the letter *bha* is the remover of fear, and the letter *ya* is remembered as Bhairavī. (36)
The seed-syllable *kubīja*, as well as *unmatta* and *rūṃ*; likewise the seed-syllable *lalitā*, the seed-syllable *huṃ*, *niḥsvabhāva*, and similarly *kāmarudra*. (37)
(19) Joined with the syllables *hūṃ hūṃ* at the beginning and likewise at the end; the letter *ḍā* [forming] *ḍākinī*, and the group beginning with *i* [forming] *kiṃkiṇī*. || 38 ||
O Supreme Lord, you are the agent through the letters of the *nivṛtti* kalā and the guardians of the field (*kṣetrapāla*).
Do not [be subject to] death, O Beloved, through the effort of the pair of letters belonging to the *amṛta* kalā. (39)
Let Mākālī, whose form is the letter *mā*, who is Bhīma-Bhairava, and the letter *ya* along with the devotees of Yama, be saluted by means of the wives of Agni (the *svāhā* ending). (40)
I bow to Kāśinātha, Ramānātha, and Yadunātha;
and to Śrī Mahābhairava and Unmatta, who are themselves free from their own burdens. 42.
With cries of "Hā! Hā! and the smoke of burnt offerings, as well as the sound of "Hu-hu," [they were] adorned with Sāṃkhya and Yoga, drinking vessels, and garlands of severed heads.
Holding a sword, a khaṭvāṅga staff, a noose, and a vajra; the lord of the Mother of the Jar (Ghaṭāmbikā);
richly adorned with the ornaments of serpents and beautified by serpent-earrings. || 43 ||

One should meditate upon Kātyāyanī Rudrā, who is richly adorned with ornaments of serpent-necklaces, wears a tiger-skin as an upper garment, holds a water-pot in her hand, and has Varuṇa as her presiding lord.
Salutation to you, the Lord of Cāmuṇḍā; salutation to you, the Lord of Vārāhī.
Salutation to you, the Lord of Caṇḍikā; salutation to you, the Lord of Brahmāṇī. || 45 ||

Salutations to you, the lord of Vaiṣṇavī, O benefactor of the three worlds! You are Kaumārī, you are the elder brother [of Kumāra], and salutations to you, Bhairava, who are like one intoxicated with power.
O Indrāṇī, you who hold the thunderbolt in your hand; homage to the Lord of Indrāṇī!
To you, the Lord of Cāmuṇḍā, O Protector, the Terrifier of the Three Worlds! (47)
I remove the Lord of Vijayā-daśamī and the destroyer of disease;
she who possesses the luster of a pearl necklace and the color of gold, being both sāttvikī and likewise rājasī.
Having heard these words from the Guru of Speech, Śaṃkara, the son of Śambhu, became Bhairava;
O Lord, he is the Bhairava of Vārāṇasī, the Bhairava of the Madman.
The man who constantly recites this *Unmatta-hṛdaya* together with its ancillaries attains his desired success and is freed from various afflictions. (50)
One should always bear in one's heart Kāmākṣā, the eternal bestower of thoughts, who destroys the afflictions caused by spirits, ghosts, and other beings, as well as by ḍākinīs. 51.
One seeking knowledge shall obtain knowledge; one seeking wealth shall obtain wealth;
one seeking liberation shall obtain liberation; and one seeking success shall attain success. (52)
He should constantly recite this at the three times of day in a cremation ground or a temple of Śiva; having performed the recitation with the mantras of the Night and the Heart-mantra of Bhairava.
I shall now proclaim that *kīlaka* and the arrangement of the *yantra*, which is complex; O you whose mind is intent on this task, listen as I explain it in detail. (54)

Hari Oṃ Tatsat. In the Pārameśvara Tantra, in the Vārāṇasī Paṭala, within the narrative of Unmattabhairava, in the dialogue between the Guru and Rudra, the Śrī-Unmattabhairavahṛdaya is completed. May there be auspiciousness.
